title: HighDimensionalStrongQuasar.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The admissible class permits nonconvex objectives; convexity and strong convexity are not required.

problem_class.label: quasar
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable, globally L-smooth, (γ,μ)-strongly quasar-convex function on ℝ^d: there exists a global minimizer x* such that f(x)+(1/γ)⟨∇f(x),x*−x⟩+(μ/2)‖x*−x‖²≤f(x*) for every x. Initially f(x0)−f(x*)≤Δ.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: One oracle returns ∇f(x) at any queried x∈ℝ^d. The supplied relative-error parameter is δ=0, so replies are exact, measurable, and independent of history and oracle seeds. Function values are not returned.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean geometry on ℝ^d, with d≥(√(L/μ)/γ)^5[Δ/(1000γ√(L/μ)ε)]³.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All parameters d,L,x0,μ,γ,Δ,ε are public; f and its minimizer are hidden. Restrictions are L,μ,ε>0, 0<γ≤1/256, 870400μ≤L, 4μ≤γ²L, and Δ≥1000γ√(L/μ)ε. The gradient is globally L-Lipschitz. Algorithms may be randomized and adaptive, with no additional algorithm restriction.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalStrongQuasar.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput and spec.valid; LongTails/Setups/RelativeGradientStrongQuasar.lean: spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm and Setup.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a point X∈ℝ^d whose objective gap f(X)−f(x*) is integrable and has expectation at most ε for a global minimizer x*. The output need not be a queried point.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalStrongQuasar.lean: spec.Output and spec.successful; LongTails/Setups/RelativeGradientStrongQuasar.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.output.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee is E[f(X)−f(x*)]≤ε over algorithm and oracle seeds under a fixed maximum number of oracle calls. Exact replies eliminate oracle randomness, but algorithm randomness remains permitted.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/RelativeGradientStrongQuasar.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence, executeWithTrace and Algorithm.law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Strongly quasar-convex exact-gradient optimization is an established formulation, but this setup imposes unusually specific parameter regimes and a dimension threshold depending jointly on conditioning, quasar convexity, initialization, and accuracy.

descriptionHtml:
High-Dimensional Strong Quasar Minimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R with an L-Lipschitz gradient, where d is the dimension and L>0. The function is strongly quasar-convex toward a global minimizer x⋆, with parameters μ>0 and 0<γ≤1/256. A given starting point x0∈Rd satisfies f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ, where Δ≥0. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈Rd with integrable objective gap satisfying EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Rdf(x). We use the Euclidean inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ and its induced norm ∥⋅∥. The algorithm receives d, L, x0, μ, γ, Δ, and ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Parameter and dimension regime). The dimension d is a nonnegative integer. In addition to the parameter ranges above, define κ=L/μ and require 870400μ≤L,4μ≤γ2L,1000γκε≤Δ,(κγ)5(Δ1000γκε)3≤d.

Assumption 2 (Smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere, and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈Rd.

Assumption 3 (Strong quasar convexity and initial gap). There exists a global minimizer x⋆∈Rd satisfying the stated initial objective-gap bound such that, for every x∈Rd, f(x)−f(x⋆)≤1γ⟨∇f(x),x−x⋆⟩−μ2∥x−x⋆∥2.

Queries may be made at any point of Rd. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must have an integrable objective gap under P and satisfy EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Jun-Kun Wang and Andre Wibisono. Continuized Acceleration for Quasar Convex Functions in Non-Convex Optimization. 2023, ICLR; preprint v1. Complexity: O(γ−1L/μlog⁡(1+Δ/(γε))) expected exact-gradient oracle calls for E[f(X)−f∗]≤ε, using continuized Nesterov acceleration stopped at a fixed continuous time.
  • Julien Hermant, Jean-François Aujol, Charles Dossal, and Aude Rondepierre. Study of the behaviour of Nesterov Accelerated Gradient in a non convex setting: the strongly quasar convex case. 2024 preprint; version used: v2, 2025. Complexity: O(γ−1L/μlog⁡(1+Δ/(γε))) fixed exact-gradient oracle calls for f(xN)−f∗≤ε, using Nesterov accelerated gradient, provided f(y)≥f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩−γμL2∥y−x∥2 for all x,y.

comparisonHtml:
Differentiable f:Rd→R has L-Lipschitz gradient and a global minimizer x⋆ satisfying f(x⋆)≥f(x)+γ−1⟨∇f(x),x⋆−x⟩+μ2∥x−x⋆∥2 for every x, with f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ. Parameters satisfy L,μ,ε>0, 0<γ≤1/256, κ≥870400, γ2κ≥4, Δ≥1000γκε, and d≥(κ/γ)5[Δ/(1000γκε)]3. The oracle returns exact gradients. The target is integrable expected gap ∫[f(xout(ω))−f(x⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε, with P the algorithm’s seed law. Under this same model, (1) and (2) match up to constants when ε≤Δ/(106γκ); for q≥2 otherwise, their ratio is at most O(log⁡κ).

import LongTails.Setups.RelativeGradientStrongQuasar
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalStrongQuasar

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  L : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  μ : ℝ
  γ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

noncomputable abbrev Params.toRelative (p : Params) :
    LongTails.Setups.RelativeGradientStrongQuasar.Params :=
  { E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d), L := p.L, x0 := p.x0, μ := p.μ, γ := p.γ, δ := 0,
    Δ := p.Δ, ε := p.ε }

noncomputable abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d) → ℝ
  Query p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Reply p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Output p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  publicInput := id
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.μ ∧ 0 < p.γ ∧ p.γ ≤ 1 / 256 ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧
    870400 * p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 4 * p.μ ≤ p.γ ^ 2 * p.L ∧
    1000 * p.γ * Real.sqrt (p.L / p.μ) * p.ε ≤ p.Δ ∧
    (Real.sqrt (p.L / p.μ) / p.γ) ^ 5 * (p.Δ / (1000 * p.γ * Real.sqrt (p.L / p.μ) * p.ε)) ^ 3 ≤ p.d
  admissible p f O := LongTails.Setups.RelativeGradientStrongQuasar.spec.admissible p.toRelative f O
  successful p f output P :=
    LongTails.Setups.RelativeGradientStrongQuasar.spec.successful p.toRelative f output P

end LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalStrongQuasar
